name: Huram-abi
overview: Huram-abi was a skilled male craftsman noted in Scripture for his unique heritage as the son of a Danite woman and a Tyrian father. His expertise in craftsmanship is highlighted in 2 Chronicles 2:13, marking him as an important artisan in the biblical narrative. No further tribal affiliations or additional notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Huram-abi means 'my father is Huram,' indicating a personal or familial connection to the name Huram. Another related name, Huram, means '[my] brother is elevated,' showing a common Semitic root and cultural significance. These names emphasize familial ties but were not given directly by God according to the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Huram-abi beyond what is noted in his unique attribute—that he is the son of a Danite woman and a Tyrian father. No other relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Huram-abi's significance lies primarily in his role as a skilled craftsman whose mixed heritage bridged Israelite and Tyrian cultures. His expertise was valued in the construction projects associated with King Solomon, reflecting God's provision of gifted artisans for the building of the temple. This underscores God's sovereign orchestration in equipping His people with the necessary skills for His purposes.
